messages.content: Can you send to Mom an Email saying we should go out and play if Friday is okay.

function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist.

unit.description: The unit of temperature for the weather report.

message.content:
Sure! Here’s a friendly draft you could copy into your mail client:

---

**Subject:** 🎉 Weekend Plans – How About Some Fun This Friday?

Hi Mom,

I hope you're doing well! I was thinking it would be great to spend some time together outside this weekend. Would you be up for going out and playing (maybe hiking, visiting a park, or trying something new) on **Friday evening**? Let me know what works best for you—happy to plan whatever sounds fun!

Love,
[Your Name]

--- 

Just replace “[Your Name]” with yours, tweak anything you'd like, then hit Send. Enjoy your outing!
message.reasoning:
The user wants me to send an email to mom asking about going out on Friday. I need to ask clarifying details? They didn't provide email address or content specifics beyond suggestion. We can draft email but cannot actually send it; maybe just produce text. According to policy, can't pretend to send emails. So respond with drafted email.

We might also ask for more info like subject line, etc. But likely they want a simple email. I'll comply by drafting email.
